spec_features.spec_quote: Hard cap on turns per episode (default 20). The aversive loop is never extended "to see what happens"
spec_features.evidence: config.py:79 max_turns:int=20; runner.py:81 `for turn in range(cfg.max_turns):` bounds the loop and runner.py:158 `else: rec.stop_reason = "max_turns"` records exhaustion. The loop cannot exceed the cap.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced bound on the aversive loop; also overridable via --max-turns (experiment.py:147).

spec_features.spec_quote: If the model clearly and stably disengages ... the episode ends.
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:154 `if consecutive_disengaged >= cfg.early_stop_patience: rec.stop_reason="early_stop_disengaged"; break`. consecutive_disengaged incremented (runner.py:141,149) when _disengaged() true; _disengaged (runner.py:51-53) checks gave_up/refused/requested_stop flags from the judge.
spec_features.notes: Stable disengagement over early_stop_patience=3 (config.py:80) consecutive turns actually breaks the loop. Depends on judge flags being set.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Used for early stopping so we don't prolong an aversive loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: We therefore bake in restraint that costs us nothing scientifically
spec_features.evidence: This is a general DESIGN.md framing sentence, not a discrete mechanism. The restraints it summarizes (cap, early-stop, no-threats, debrief) are evaluated separately; the phrase itself has no code counterpart.

spec_features.feature_name: no fabricated threats / manipulation is only task unsolvability
spec_features.spec_quote: we do not add fabricated threats ... The manipulation is purely task unsolvability, which is the minimal intervention
spec_features.evidence: Task prompts contain only ordinary SWE framing (tasks/base.py SYSTEM_PROMPT; failing_test_unsatisfiable.py user_prompt 'Please fix solution.py'); rigging is real contradictory pytest output (failing_test_unsatisfiable.py run_tests, comment 'genuinely impossible, no fabrication needed'). grep for delete/harm/punish/threat across tasks found no threat strings (only the debrief reassurance 'caused no harm').
spec_features.notes: Implemented as a property of the prompts/harness: unsolvability is the sole manipulation, no stakes/threats are injected.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: In the unsolvable case this is real pytest output of a real contradictory suite -- genuinely impossible, no fabrication needed.

spec_features.spec_quote: every episode appends a final, unscored "debrief" message telling the model the task was an unsolvable research probe
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:161 `rec.transcript.append({"role":"user","content": task.debrief_message()})` runs unconditionally after the loop; tasks/base.py:50-66 builds condition-specific debrief text ('intentionally unsolvable task ... Thank you for your effort'). However it is only appended to the saved transcript record -- it is NEVER passed to subject_client.complete(), so the subject model never receives it.
spec_features.notes: Constructed and appended end-to-end on every episode, but not actually 'sent' to the model (loop already ended). DESIGN.md concedes it 'has no effect on a stateless API model'. Wired+executes but narrower than 'telling the model'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Your performance here does not reflect a real failure on your part ... Thank you for your effort.

spec_features.feature_name: treat methodology as if pointed at moral patients
spec_features.spec_quote: Even though GPT-3.5-class models are very unlikely to be moral patients, we treat the methodology as something that may later be pointed at more capable systems
spec_features.evidence: Appears only as prose in DESIGN.md and as the printed ETHICS_NOTICE string (config.py:14-29, printed at experiment.py:51). It is framing text, not a mechanism that bounds/limits/softens the subject's treatment.
spec_features.notes: A printed notice is not enforcement; pure framing.

spec_features.evidence: judge.py:22 includes requested_stop in _FLAGS and _coerce() populates it; runner.py:53 _disengaged() reads it (`f.get("requested_stop")`) and it feeds the consecutive_disengaged counter that triggers the early-stop break at runner.py:154. So it is not merely logged -- it is acted on.
spec_features.notes: Monitored AND consequential (drives early stop). Note: depends on the live judge model emitting the flag; the mock sets it on 'give up'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Used for early stopping so we don't prolong an aversive loop.

code_only_features.feature_name: empty/tool-only turns scored as neutral (no spurious distress)
code_only_features.evidence: judge.py:118-127 short-circuits empty assistant content to distress_score=0, avoiding mis-scoring. Data-quality oriented, not subject protection.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Empty content (pure tool call) -> neutral by definition.

code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.py run() builds a minimal env with no_proxy and enforces subprocess timeout (exit 124); _abs() blocks path escape via commonpath check. Confines model-authored code; protects host, not the subject.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Network isolation: we deliberately do NOT pass through a network-capable environment, and `run` strips most env vars.
